action: Install Check Point's November Jumbo Hotfix on all Management Servers and Security Gateways, starting with internet-facing Mobile Access deployments. Hunt for the published indicators and ask Check Point Support for an exposure assessment.
exec: A fix existed a week before the attacks; only unpatched gateways were hit, and a small number in one region were wiped.
plain: Check Point says attackers broke into about two dozen of its security devices that lacked a fix issued on October 23. Some Israeli organisations had data wiped; later attacks in other countries were not destructive.

key_findings: Attackers used PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619, CVSS 9.2) in the Mobile Access Portal for unauthenticated code execution, then CVE-2026-123039 to become root.
Exploitation began October 30, about a week after the PHP2Shell hotfix of October 23; the advisory counts a couple of dozen compromised unpatched systems.
The first wave targeted Israeli organisations and was destructive in a limited number of cases; a second wave from November 2 reached organisations in several countries with no destruction reported.
Tools included the TSGA backdoor, a TSProxy library, PHP webshells, a network scanner and a wiper that was also run on a VMware ESXi host reached over SSH.
Check Point Research links the tooling to the PhiliKit framework but does not attribute the campaign with confidence and raises a possible false flag.
report.publisher: Check Point (security advisory and Check Point Research)
recommendations: Install the November Jumbo Hotfix on all Management Servers and Security Gateways as soon as possible.
Hunt for the published indicators, including a process masquerading as a Check Point daemon and unexplained gaps in firewall logs.
Contact Check Point Support for exposure assessment; absence of an indicator match does not rule out compromise.

summary: Check Point says attackers chained the PHP2Shell flaws in the Mobile Access Portal with a Gaia privilege escalation to gain root on unpatched gateways from October 30. A first wave hit Israeli organisations and wiped some systems, including a VMware ESXi host; a second wave from November 2 exploited gateways in several countries without destruction. About two dozen unpatched systems were compromised.
title: Unpatched Check Point gateways wiped in PHP2Shell attacks

validation.note: Reviewed against the original Check Point report.
